title: How Much Does Metal Stud Framing Cost in Vaughan?
description: Prepare a Vaughan metal stud framing quote with clear measurements, scope, inclusions, exclusions, and practical steps for comparing contractor costs.
html:
How much does metal stud framing cost in Vaughan? There is no reliable single price because the total depends on wall area, stud and track specifications, openings, height, access, installation scope, and project coordination. This guide focuses on preparing and comparing Vaughan framing quotations, not on applying a broad market rate to every project.

Budget the work by separating material supply, installation labour, and broader renovation items, then request a quote using consistent drawings, dimensions, quantities, and inclusions.

What a Vaughan metal stud framing quote actually represents

A metal stud framing price can describe very different scopes. A supply-only quote covers products, while an installed-framing quote may add labour, fasteners, equipment, delivery, and coordination. A broader renovation quote may also include demolition, insulation, drywall, finishing, painting, electrical, or plumbing.

For a meaningful budget, ask which of these scopes you are comparing:

  • Material supply: steel studs, track, fasteners, clips, channels, and specified accessories.
  • Framing installation: labour and site work required to assemble the specified framing system.
  • Complete renovation work: framing plus other trades and finishes defined in the proposal.

Dass Metal Products presents itself as a manufacturer of building products. Clarify at the outset whether you are requesting framing materials, product guidance, or a broader scope arranged with a contractor.

Break the quote into materials, labour, and project scope

Steel framing is not automatically expensive or inexpensive in isolation. The answer depends on the wall assembly, material quantity, installation labour, and site conditions.

Quote itemWhat it may coverWhat to verify
Steel studs and trackStuds, standard track, deep track, slotted track, or other specified profilesProfile, gauge, dimensions, lengths, quantity, and application
AccessoriesFasteners, clips, channels, bracing, trims, or other componentsWhether accessories are included or separate
Installation labourLayout, cutting, fastening, framing, and site adjustmentsWhether framing only or finish-ready preparation is covered
Delivery and mobilizationTransport, unloading, setup, and return visitsDelivery location, access, quantities, and phased shipments
Supervision and coordinationSite management, drawing coordination, and trade communicationWhether this is included, itemized, or excluded
Shop drawings or submittalsProduct documentation, layout information, or project drawingsRequired deliverables and review responsibility
Cleanup and disposalOffcuts, packaging, debris removal, or final cleaningWho removes waste and what “clean” means
Overhead, profit, and taxesBusiness costs, contractor margin, and applicable taxesWhether each amount is included or separate

A price per square foot, linear foot, hour, or complete project is meaningful only when the measured scope is identical. A material-only price cannot be compared fairly with an installed price that includes delivery, supervision, cleanup, and coordination.

The measurements and conditions that change the estimate

Framing quantity usually begins with wall length and height, not floor area. Two Vaughan projects with the same floor area can require very different amounts of steel framing if one has more rooms, longer partitions, higher ceilings, or more openings.

Wall dimensions and layout

Record each wall’s length and height, then identify corners, intersections, jogs, soffits, bulkheads, doors, windows, service openings, and areas needing additional framing. Openings reduce some stud quantity but add detailing around the opening.

Stud role, spacing, and track

Identify whether each wall is a non-load-bearing partition, shaftwall, exterior or structural condition, or specialized assembly. Stud width, gauge, spacing, track, bridging, bracing, and deflection details should follow the drawings and project requirements.

A head-of-wall condition may require standard track, deep track, or slotted deflection track. Tall walls, load-supporting walls, and unusual movement conditions require more careful specification than straightforward partitions.

Site access and sequencing

Restricted loading areas, occupied buildings, stairs, long carrying distances, limited storage, phased access, and tight delivery windows can increase handling and mobilization. Tall walls, steel beams, and difficult overhead conditions can also change the installation sequence.

A worksheet for preparing a Vaughan framing estimate

Complete these fields before requesting a quotation. The worksheet does not create a price by itself. It gives the supplier or contractor the information needed to measure, select, and price the correct scope.

Project inputYour information
Project typeCommercial interior, basement, tenant improvement, renovation, shaftwall, or other
Floor areaApproximate area, used only as background context
Wall scheduleEach wall’s length, height, location, and type
OpeningsDoor, window, service, and access opening sizes and quantities
Stud spacingSpacing shown on drawings or required by design
Stud specificationWidth, gauge, finish, load role, and performance requirement
Track and accessoriesStandard or special track, clips, channels, bracing, and fasteners
Ceiling conditionFixed, suspended, deflecting, sloped, irregular, or unconfirmed
AccessLoading area, floor level, storage, occupied spaces, lifts, and working hours
ScheduleDelivery date, installation sequence, and phasing
Requested scopeSupply only, supply and installation, or coordinated framing
DocumentsDrawings, wall types, specifications, details, revisions, and takeoff

Use floor area to describe the project, but do not use it as the framing quantity. Measure the actual partitions, perimeter walls, openings, and special conditions shown in the plans.

Two illustrative scenarios: straightforward partition versus basement conditions

The examples below are hypothetical estimating exercises, not Vaughan market rates or Dass Metal Products pricing. They show why a measured scope produces a better quotation request than a headline price.

Scenario one: a straightforward interior partition

Imagine a hypothetical non-load-bearing partition 80 linear feet long and 10 feet high, with two standard door openings. The request identifies the wall detail, required stud spacing and gauge, and asks for separate material and installation figures.

The quantity review would identify the stud run, top and bottom track, opening framing, fasteners, delivery requirements, and any waste allowance. Labour would cover layout, cutting, fastening, opening details, cleanup, and access.

This is stronger than saying “price 800 square feet of framing.” That figure describes one wall face, but not openings, track, accessories, installation conditions, or drywall.

Scenario two: a hypothetical 1,500-square-foot basement

A 1,500-square-foot basement cannot be given a dependable framing price from floor area alone. The estimate needs the perimeter, interior partition lengths, ceiling height, foundation conditions, columns, beams, mechanical rooms, stairs, doors, windows, insulation requirements, and access route.

A basement with a simple open layout and clear delivery access differs from one with several rooms, boxed columns, low clearance, existing services, irregular foundation walls, and limited storage. The second project may require more layout, cutting, coordination, handling, and return visits.

Ask for the basement estimate to separate framing from insulation, vapour control, drywall, finishing, electrical, plumbing, demolition, disposal, permits, and painting.

Metal studs versus wood: compare the cost drivers, not just the material price

Wood studs are not universally cheaper, and metal studs are not universally more expensive. The better choice depends on moisture exposure, dimensions, performance criteria, labour method, tools, schedule, and the complete assembly.

Decision factorMetal studsWood studs
Material costDepends on profile, gauge, dimensions, quantity, accessories, and deliveryDepends on grade, dimensions, quantity, availability, and delivery
Installation costDepends on layout, cutting, fastening, tools, openings, and crew familiarityDepends on cutting, fastening, handling, openings, and crew familiarity
Moisture exposureMay suit applications where ordinary moisture-related movement is a concern, subject to the assemblyRequires careful material selection and moisture management
Dimensional stabilityConsistent manufactured profiles support layout and finish requirementsCan vary with material condition and moisture changes
Fire-rated constructionMust be selected as part of a tested or specified assemblyMust also be selected as part of the applicable assembly
Structural requirementsLoad-bearing or tall-wall conditions require the correct design, gauge, spacing, and connectionsLoad and span control species, grade, size, spacing, and connections
Typical fitInterior partitions, commercial framing, and specialized steel-profile assembliesApplications suited to the design, site method, and project requirements

For fire safety, cost, or strength, compare complete assemblies and project requirements rather than relying on the material name.

What framing does not include in a basement or re-drywall budget

Framing is only one part of many renovations. A basement or re-drywall budget may also include demolition, disposal, insulation, vapour control, drywall board, taping, finishing, painting, electrical, plumbing, HVAC work, permits, protection, and final cleaning.

A 2,000-square-foot house cannot receive a useful re-drywall framing price from floor area alone. The estimator needs wall and ceiling surface area, room heights, existing framing condition, demolition, openings, repairs, access, and the exact work included.

How to request and compare metal stud framing quotes in Vaughan

Send the same information to each supplier or contractor so responses describe equivalent work.

  1. Provide current documents. Include drawings, wall types, details, specifications, revisions, and any takeoff.
  2. List the measured scope. State wall lengths, heights, openings, room count, perimeter conditions, and special features.
  3. Define the wall role. Identify non-load-bearing, load-bearing, shaftwall, deflection, acoustic, fire-rated, exterior, or other requirements.
  4. Specify components. Identify studs, track, fasteners, clips, channels, bracing, trims, and documents.
  5. Choose the pricing scope. Ask for supply only, installation only, or a combined price.
  6. Describe site conditions. Include access, loading, storage, floor level, working hours, occupied areas, lifts, beams, and phasing.
  7. Request inclusions and exclusions. Ask about delivery, mobilization, supervision, shop drawings, waste, cleanup, taxes, and changes.
  8. Compare like with like. Check quantities, specifications, schedule assumptions, and finish-ready boundaries.

Mobilization, supervision, shop drawings, cleanup, delivery, overhead, profit, taxes, and return visits become problems when they are missing from the original assumptions.

Questions to ask before accepting a framing quotation

How much would it cost to frame a 1,500-square-foot basement in Vaughan?

There is no dependable basement framing price from 1,500 square feet alone. Measure the perimeter and partitions, then account for height, openings, columns, beams, foundation conditions, access, and scope.

Is steel framing expensive compared with wood framing?

Not automatically. Compare equivalent scopes with the same dimensions, openings, accessories, delivery, and installation assumptions.

How much of a 2,000-square-foot re-drywall project is actually framing?

Only the portions requiring new partitions, repairs, furring, or replacement framing are framing work. Request separate lines for demolition, board installation, finishing, painting, and other trades.

Is metal stud framing priced by square foot, linear foot, hourly labour, or project?

Any of those units can be used, but none is meaningful without a defined scope. Linear feet suit measured walls, square feet can describe wall or project area, hourly labour describes time, and a project price combines listed assumptions.

What should be included in a Vaughan metal stud framing quote?

A clear quote should identify stud and track specifications, quantities, accessories, delivery, installation labour, mobilization, supervision, submittals, cleanup, taxes, schedule assumptions, exclusions, and change-order terms. It should also state whether drywall, insulation, finishing, demolition, disposal, electrical, plumbing, permits, and painting are outside the framing scope.

Prepare the drawings, wall measurements, openings, wall functions, access details, schedule, and requested scope before seeking pricing. For general product and quotation guidance, review Dass Metal Products’ steel framing products and provide the project information needed for a meaningful response.
